name: Can laminate, thermofoil, or factory-finished cabinets be refinished, or will the new coating peel?

mainEntity.name: Can laminate, thermofoil, or factory-finished cabinets be refinished, or will the new coating peel?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, but the surface must be compatible with the proposed coating and prepared correctly. Context: Factory finishes, laminate, thermofoil, and previously painted cabinets behave differently, and some damaged surfaces cannot be made durable with coating alone. A bonding system may be needed, but product selection should follow an inspection rather than a guess. Key factors: - Peeling edges, swollen fiberboard, and delamination are warning signs. - Smooth factory surfaces need thorough cleaning and deglossing or sanding. - Heat and moisture near dishwashers and sinks increase risk. Practical guidance: Tell the contractor exactly what the doors are made of and disclose prior paint, repairs, or failed refinishing. Ask for a small test area or sample before approving the full kitchen. Elite Remodeling & Design can determine whether refinishing is appropriate or whether a different cabinet treatment is more dependable.
acceptedAnswer.description: Some laminate, thermofoil, and factory-finished cabinets can be recoated, but adhesion depends on the material, condition, preparation, and coating system. Peeling edges, swelling, and delamination may require replacement or refacing instead.
